prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
# 10 Stock Ideas for Trying to Beat the S&P 500

Nobody can reliably pick stocks that beat the index over a single year. In most years, over half of professional large-cap fund managers trail the S&P 500 (per S&P's SPIVA reports), and over 10+ years about 85–90% do. Over one year, luck matters more than skill. Also, my knowledge ends in May 2026, so I don't know current prices, valuations, or news from the last few months. Treat these as ideas to research, not personalized advice.

## The 10 ideas

| # | Company (Ticker) | Why it could outperform | Main risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Growing Google Cloud, Gemini AI models, its own AI chips (TPUs), and YouTube. It has often been cheaper relative to earnings than other megacaps. | AI chatbots taking search traffic; antitrust rulings |
| 2 | **Microsoft (MSFT)** | Azure cloud growth, AI products sold to businesses, very steady profits | High AI data-center spending hurting profit margins |
| 3 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | AWS cloud recovery, a fast-growing ad business, rising retail margins | Heavy spending; consumer slowdown |
| 4 | **TSMC (TSM)** | Makes nearly all leading-edge AI chips for Nvidia, Apple, AMD and others | China–Taiwan tensions; tariffs |
| 5 | **Broadcom (AVGO)** | Custom AI chips for hyperscalers and AI networking equipment, plus VMware software income | High valuation; reliance on a few big customers |
| 6 | **Vertiv (VRT)** | Power and cooling equipment for data centers | Very sensitive to any slowdown in AI spending; volatile stock |
| 7 | **GE Vernova (GEV)** | Gas turbines and power-grid equipment, with electricity demand rising | High valuation; losses in its wind business |
| 8 | **Eli Lilly (LLY)** | Leads in obesity and diabetes drugs (tirzepatide, and oral orforglipron) | Drug-price pressure; competition; high valuation |
| 9 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | Best-in-class bank; adds balance outside tech | Credit losses in a recession |
| 10 | **Intuitive Surgical (ISRG)** | Dominates robotic surgery, and most of its revenue repeats (instruments and service) | High valuation; newer competing robots |

## Problems with this list

1. **It's heavily tied to AI.** Six or seven of these names depend on AI spending continuing. If that spending cools, they could fall together and trail the index badly. For more balance, swap one or two for other sectors, such as consumer staples, energy, or industrials.
2. **Some picks barely differ from the index.** Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon and Broadcom are already large S&P 500 holdings. To beat the index, you have to own something different from it. Those four mostly move with the market, while names like VRT, GEV and ISRG are real bets away from it.
3. **Concentration works both ways.** Ten stocks can beat the S&P 500 by 15%, or trail it by 15%.

## A more practical approach: "core and satellite"

- **Core (70–80%):** a low-cost S&P 500 index fund, such as VOO, IVV or SPLG.
- **Satellite (20–30%):** your stock picks, split equally among them.
- **Set rules in advance:** decide how you'll handle rebalancing and when you'd sell a pick if its reason for owning it no longer holds.
- **Measure honestly:** after 12 months, compare your total return with the S&P 500, including dividends.

**Before buying, check:**
- Current valuations (price-to-earnings compared with each stock's own history)
- The latest earnings reports
- Taxes: in the US, gains on shares held under a year are taxed at higher rates
- That you have an emergency fund and won't need this money soon

If you share your risk tolerance, your account type, or sectors you want to avoid or favor, I can adjust the list.
